facts.text: I've had a cough that won't go away.
Mostly in my hips and lower back.

facts.item: how long the symptoms have been going on
facts.text: All of this has been going on for the past 2 months.
Before the cough started, I considered myself in good general health.
I take clopamide every day for my blood pressure.
Four months ago I went on a hiking trip near Phoenix, Arizona.
I haven't lost any significant weight.

findings.name: lung examination
findings.result: Inspection: no obvious distress or cyanosis. Auscultation: mildly reduced breath sounds on the right lower side. Percussion: dullness over the right middle lobe. Palpation: mildly increased fremitus over the right lower chest.

findings.name: musculoskeletal examination
findings.result: Inspection: no visible joint deformities. Palpation: tenderness in the lower back and hips.

findings.name: chest X-ray
findings.result: Right-sided consolidation in the lower right lung.

findings.name: chest CT
findings.result: Irregular opacity in the right middle lobe measuring 3.8 cm x 3.0 cm; small right-sided pleural effusion; mild hilar adenopathy.

findings.name: lung biopsy
findings.result: Necrotic granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and spherules with endospores.

findings.name: complete blood count
findings.result: Hemoglobin 12.9 g/dL; leukocyte count 9,300/mm³; platelet count 167,000/mm³.

findings.name: periodic acid-Schiff and silver methenamine stains

source_issues: Hemoglobin is given as '12.9 mg/dL' (unit typo for g/dL).
Lesion location differs slightly between studies: chest X-ray 'lower right lung', CT and percussion 'right middle lobe', auscultation 'right lower side'.
The patient is febrile (38.6°C) and tachycardic, but the history and ROS do not mention fever; left unknown in the patient record.
The PAS/silver methenamine and acid-fast stains are listed as laboratory tests without a specimen.
notes: The 2-month duration applies to the cough, joint aches and malaise, so it is a standalone fact (f005). The joint locations are a child (f003), not complete ('particularly').
'Considered himself in general good health prior to the onset of the cough' is f006 (health problems before the cough, absent); his hypertension is recorded separately (f007), as in the source.
The multivitamin is not explicitly daily in the source ('takes clopamide daily along with a multivitamin'), so f009 has no frequency.
Hemoglobin, leukocyte and platelet counts are grouped as a complete blood count; the ESR and the stains are separate records.
The gold word 'fever' is kept out of the patient facts; no fever fact exists in the patient fragments.

extras.objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with chronic cough, aching joints, and malaise.
